title: autoscale-safety-fuse: prevent runaway autoscaler from mass-evicting tenants
author: Aditi Raman
description: Context: A customer incident (SUP-9482) revealed a rare autoscaler feedback loop where aggressive scale-down cycles during a region-wide transient caused the autoscaler to decide in rapid succession to reclaim capacity and trigger tenant evictions. Evicted tenants incurred cold-start penalties and a storm of reconnects, which amplified the autoscaler's signals and led to cascading evictions across a small set of co-located nodes. This PR introduces a runtime "safety fuse" in the autoscaler and an eviction guard in the serving scheduler that together: 1) detect runaway oscillation patterns, 2) convert aggressive eviction decisions into timeboxed admission throttles (load-shedding and prefetch backoff) instead of immediate evictions, and 3) allow safe, rollback-free remediation by exposing a short-lived runtime flag and conservative defaults. Repro: internal incident runbook reproduced the oscillation by running synthetic latency bursts against a pinned tenant cohort and toggling scale anchors. The sequence of decisions shown in the incident trace made it clear that eviction thresholds were reached repeatedly in <2 minute windows. Solution summary: - Autoscaler: add a two-stage fuse (fast detection + rate-limited enforcement). On fast detection, autoscaler moves into a protective window where scale-downs larger than N% are rate-limited and tenant eviction intent is replaced with an admission-shim proposal. - Scheduler/eviction: add EvictionGuard that will decline mass evictions when the controlplane reports a safety fuse state and instead apply admission tags (shed_level: light|moderate) with an associated TTL. - Admission path: implement lightweight shed hints that ingress honors to apply token-bucket based admission throttles per-tenant and per-route. - Telemetry: emit autoscaler.fuse.event, eviction_guard.decision, admission.shed_level with tenant_id and cohort tags. - Runtime controls: feature flag hotfix.autoscale_safety_fuse (on by default for hotfix rollout) and a config knob autoscale.max_scale_down_pct_per_window. Rollout plan: - Canary (region: us-west-2) with 10% of traffic for 30m, observe eviction counts, latency P95, and reconnection spikes. - Gradual 3x expansion with monitoring gates. - Full enable if no regression; otherwise revert flag (no DB migration required). Testing: - Unit tests added for fuse transition logic and eviction guard heuristics. - Integration test harness simulates autoscaler loop with deterministic random seeds and validates that eviction rate drops and shed signals increase instead. - New e2e test that runs a synthetic tenant cohort under bursty load for 20 minutes. Observability: dashboards added for fuse state, number of aborted evictions, and shed_rate_by_tenant. Alerts: added temporary alert AUTO-FUSE-ANOMALY for >5 fuse activations / 10m during canary. Followups: - (ENG-1830) evaluate longer-term autoscaler policy (learning-based dampening). - Remove the temporary alert after one successful release window. Checklist: - [x] Repro case in incident runbook updated - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry and dashboards - [x] Runtime feature flag and safe default - [x] Canary rollout instructions attached in PR thread Links: runbook: https://linear.app/support/incident/SUP-9482, internal dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/company/d/auto-fuse, design note: https://linear.app/eng/notes/ENG-1827

release_notes: Hotfix: Prevents a runaway autoscaler feedback loop that could result in mass tenant evictions by adding a safety fuse and eviction guard. Default turned on for Canary in us-west-2. No SDK changes. Users may notice fewer cold-start evictions during transient regional load spikes.
notes_for_ops: During canary, watch panels: autoscaler.fuse.event, eviction_guard.aborted_evictions, admission.shed_rate_by_tenant. If ALERT AUTO-FUSE-ANOMALY fires > 3 times in first 6h, flip feature flag hotfix.autoscale_safety_fuse=false and notify on-call SRE. Revert path: disable runtime flag; no code rollback required.
